raw_response:
I'm 71 this year, been farming for 50 years. My son works in a factory over in Handan, sends some money back when he can. It's mostly me and my wife on our 15 mu farm — well, 15 mu and a bit. We have about 10 mu in wheat-maize double cropping, and the rest, about 5 mu, is cotton. I only went to primary school, so I don't read those agricultural manuals. I go by what I've seen with my own eyes and what my neighbors do.

The **wheat** went in last October, same time as every year. I plowed after taking out the maize, then harrowed and planted. I put down about 40 kg of compound fertilizer per mu as base — almost a full bag. In March at jointing, I spread about 20 kg of urea per mu, half a bag. The wheat looks alright, not the best I've seen, not the worst. I've irrigated twice already with the well pump. Pumping costs money, about 15 yuan each time, so I only water when the soil is really dry and the wheat starts looking thirsty. I'll probably do one more irrigation in May if it doesn't rain. I sprayed herbicide last autumn and fungicide this spring when I saw a bit of rust on the lower leaves — better to spend 30 yuan per mu on spray than lose half the crop. I hire the combine for harvest in early June — 60 yuan per mu, done in a day. I hope for about 400 kg per mu. I could put more fertilizer and push for 500 kg, but that costs more and if the weather turns bad in May, I lose money. Better safe. At my age, I don't gamble.

**Maize** goes in right after wheat harvest, mid-June. Sometimes only 3-4 days between crops, no time for deep plowing. I buy hybrid seed from the dealer in town, 50 yuan per mu. I put about 30 kg of compound fertilizer in the holes when planting, then topdress with 15 kg of urea when the plants are knee-high. I'll irrigate once at planting if it's dry, and maybe once in July if the rains don't come. Two sprays — herbicide right after planting, insecticide if I see corn borers. I expect about 450 kg per mu. The maize mostly takes care of itself in summer, which is good because cotton is busy then.

**Cotton** is the hardest work. I plant it now in late April. I use about 30 kg of compound fertilizer per mu at planting, then 15 kg of urea when it starts flowering in July. Cotton needs spraying every 10 days or so for bollworm and aphids — that's the biggest cost, about 80 yuan per mu just for chemicals. I irrigate twice, same as maize. The real problem is picking in September and October. My wife and I can't bend down all day anymore — our backs hurt. I have to hire women from the village, 100 yuan per day. That's expensive but there's no choice. I keep these 5 mu of cotton because the lint price was decent last year, but honestly, if my health gets worse I'll switch it all to wheat-maize. Cotton is too much work for an old man. I expect about 200 kg of lint per mu if the bugs don't get bad.

Everything together costs me about 10,000 yuan. My son helps with some cash, but I don't like to ask. I use what I have in hand. If I have extra money, I might buy a bit more fertilizer, but I never borrow from the bank. Sleep is more important than a bigger harvest.
